chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Miss Callie Frost's audition and a busy schedule, about 1927
summary: A college-connected patron hears the family band, and the group gets three or four gigs a week; Tate is 12 or 13.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So I says, "Okay." But anyway, they were all there and I had them up and they all come up and people all gave them a standing ovation. So I told them, I said, "Well, this is it. This is where we all started and these are the ones. Thank God they're still hanging in there, you know?" And there was a lady by the name of Miss Callie Frost . She had a daughter by the name of Jack Frost and Dorothy Frost. She really started it all. One Christmas -- she'd heard about the band. You know, we weren't -- playing little gigs and things here and there. But around one Christmas, she came and we, you know, did an audition for her down to my cousin's house and she just flipped over the band. She just went crazy over it. She was affiliated with the colleges and we played for her and after that, we were in. We were doing like three and four gigs a week, you know, like --
Yeah, about 13. I was between 12, 13, something --
And you had been playing for about --
Well, I was really trying to learn then.
See, that's when I was really getting into it.
